newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian oil group calls for fewer state exports.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil group calls for fewer state exports.

text.p: Russian oil exports under federal programmes must be slashed to protect big oil firms from small, corrupt trading operations, Vladimir Medvedev, president of the Union of Oil and Gas Industrialists, said on Wednesday.

Medvedev, also chairman of the small centrist Russian Regions party in the State Duma lower house of parliament, told a news conference he had discussed the issue with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin at the end of last year.
"Of course there is a need to preserve some kind of federal programme," he said. "But we agreed in principle that it should be no more than 23 to 25 million tonnes," Medvedev said.
About 20 decrees call for federal programme oil exports to rise to 60 to 70 million tonnes in 1997.
Federal programme exports in 1996 were originally targeted by the government at 71 million tonnes, although eventually they were scaled back to 27.5 million.
Domestic oil producers accounted for less than 20 percent of that, or around 5.3 million tonnes.
Under the federal programmes, the government signs decrees every year authorising companies to export certain amounts of crude to finance state investment programmes.
Federal programme exporters -- most of them trading firms rather than producers -- keep some of the proceeds, getting rich on the difference between domestic and world oil prices.

"There are a lot of companies playing the difference between internal and external oil prices to make their profits, and they will use any means, that is to say corruption and blackmail, to get access (to federal programmes)," Medvedev said.

Medvedev's comments add to the chorus of senior Russian oil officials and executives keen to crack down on the amount of exports under federal programme system, and the number of oil exporters in general.
In January Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov told Russian oil executives in Siberia that the government was preparing to limit the number of companies exporting oil.
And the president of Russia's largest oil company LUKoil, Vagit Alekperov, was quoted by Interfax as saying producers, not traders, should deliver oil abroad.
Russia exported just over a third of its oil outside the Commonwealth of Independent States in 1996. Non-CIS exports rose nine percent to 105 million tonnes (around 2.1 million barrels per day).
